english.title: Move / restrict the movement of a motor vehicle by any means intending to prevent / inhibit removal
english.standardoffencewording: On **(..SPECIFY DATE..) at **(..SPECIFY TOWNSHIP..), without lawful authority, moved or restricted the movement of a motor vehicle, namely **(..SPECIFY VEHICLE MAKE AND INDEX NUMBER..), intending to prevent or inhibit the removal of the vehicle by a person otherwise entitled to remove it
english.legislation: Contrary to section 54(1)(b) and (5) of the Protection of Freedoms Act 2012.

english.notes:
(i) Section54(2) provides that the express or implied consent (whether or not legallybinding) of a person otherwise entitled to remove the vehicle to theimmobilisation, movement or restriction concerned is not lawful authority forthe purposes of subsection (1).
(ii) Section 54(3) however states that, where the restriction of the movementof the vehicle is by means of a fixed barrier and the barrier was present(whether or not lowered into place or otherwise restricting movement) when thevehicle was parked, any express or implied consent (whether or not legallybinding) of the driver of the vehicle to the restriction is, for the purposesof subsection (1), lawful authority for the restriction.
(iii) Section 54(4) states that a person who is entitled to remove a vehiclecannot commit an offence under this section in relation to that vehicle.
(iv) Section 54(6) In this section "motor vehicle" means amechanically propelled vehicle or a vehicle designed or adapted for towing by amechanically propelled vehicle.

other.penalty:
Summary: Afine not exceeding the statutory maximum.
Indictment: A fine.

Time limit for prosecutions:
None

On the 12th March 2015 the limit on fines imposed by a Magistrates’ court was removed – as such, the potential fine on summary conviction in relation to an offence committed after this date is unlimited.
